lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Cerberus. Since we’re family — I’m a dog myself, after all — tell me, by the Styx: what was Socrates like when he came down here? I assume, being divine, you don’t only bark. You can speak human when you feel like it.

lines.speaker: Cerberus
lines.text: From a distance, Menippus, he looked completely steady. Face under control, not at all afraid of death — or at least very keen that the people standing outside the entrance should think so.

lines.speaker: Cerberus
lines.text: But once he bent down into the opening and saw the dark — and I, since he was still hesitating, took him by the foot with my teeth and pulled him down by the hemlock — he howled like a baby. Cried for his children. Fell apart in every possible direction.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: So the man was a sophist, then. He didn’t really despise the business.

lines.speaker: Cerberus
lines.text: No. He just saw it was unavoidable, so he put on a brave face — as if he were choosing, willingly, what he had to suffer anyway. The audience was meant to admire him.

lines.speaker: Cerberus
lines.text: And really I could say the same about the whole class. Up to the mouth of the pit: bold, courageous men. Inside: the audit is exact.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: And how did I seem to you when I came down?

lines.speaker: Cerberus
lines.text: You alone, Menippus, came in a manner worthy of the breed. You and Diogenes before you. Not compelled, not shoved — voluntary. Laughing. Telling everyone else to keep wailing.
